tagline: Nineteen miles of the old road west, and four Julesburgs.
intro: The loop starts at the Colorado Welcome Center in Julesburg, on the north side of the South Platte a little short of the Nebraska line, and is done in 19 miles. It is the shortest byway in the state.

The valley was the main road west. Here the Overland stage line left the Oregon-California trail, and the Pony Express kept its only Colorado home station. In January 1865 a thousand Cheyenne, Arapaho and Lakota warriors attacked Julesburg in revenge for Sand Creek, and in February they came back and burned it. There have been four Julesburgs in all, and markers stand at each townsite.

moments.title: Julesburg
moments.text: In 1867 the Union Pacific made it an end-of-track town of some 4,000 workers, and an Army colonel found that only six of its 127 graves held natural deaths.

moments.title: Fort Sedgwick
moments.text: Begun in 1864 as a couple of sod huts, the post paid as much as $100 a cord for firewood, there being not a tree for 50 miles.
